Radiology: Radiology encompasses diagnostic imaging modalities including chest X-ray interpretation for respiratory conditions and pneumoperitoneum detection, radiation safety practices such as patient exposure reduction and beam filtration, dental radiography involving material radiopacity and film processing, radiation biology mechanisms of tissue sensitivity and cell death, and technical domains like image quality optimization, grid application, and infection control in digital radiography systems.
Social & Preventive Medicine: Social & Preventive Medicine integrates epidemiological study designs (case-control, cohort), biostatistical analysis (confidence intervals, odds ratios, ROC curves), public health programs (NCD, RNTCP), vaccine efficacy, disease surveillance (AFP, HIV), and evaluation of preventive interventions, screening test validity, and population-level health policy through statistical modeling and program assessment.
Forensic Medicine: Forensic Medicine addresses brain death determination, forensic analysis of traumatic injuries (gunshot wounds, bite marks, inhalation burns, postmortem trauma), fetal age assessment, and child abuse identification. It integrates toxicological evaluations (poisoning, venom effects), medico-legal frameworks (autopsy protocols, criminal procedure codes), and injury pattern analysis (blast, chemical burns), alongside legal standards for abuse reporting and forensic documentation.
Ophthalmology: Ophthalmology specializing in diabetic retinopathy screening and ETDRS grading, glaucoma pharmacology and IOP management, neuro-ophthalmological disorders including internuclear ophthalmoplegia and trochlear nerve palsy, surgical indications such as evisceration, corneal pathology, genetic cataracts, and optic pathway diseases, with clinical and experimental correlates.
Microbiology: Microbiology encompasses bacterial pathogens (e.g., N. gonorrhoeae, Staphylococcus aureus, Vibrio cholerae) with resistance mechanisms, viral infections (Hepatitis B, HIV, measles), parasitic diseases (malaria, helminths), fungal diagnostics (beta-1,3-D glucan testing), vaccine immunology (PPV-23, Mw), biofilm-mediated antibiotic resistance, sterilization techniques, hypersensitivity reactions, and diagnostic methods for infectious diseases including molecular and serological assays.
Gynaecology & Obstetrics: Gynaecology & Obstetrics focuses on prenatal diagnosis of Down syndrome and intrauterine growth restriction, maternal-fetal medicine including Hepatitis B transmission and diabetes management, postpartum hemorrhage management, DIC diagnosis, preterm labor interventions, gonadal dysgenesis, and reproductive endocrinology addressing infertility and genetic disorders.
ENT: ENT academic knowledge addresses laryngeal carcinoma treatments with stridor and staging, auditory system effects of noise and WHO hearing loss classification, paranasal sinus development and anatomy, hearing assessment via Rinne’s and Weber’s tests, and airway management involving cranial nerves and auditory pathways.
Skin: Skin academic knowledge includes allergic contact dermatitis, drug-induced reactions, infection-related cutaneous manifestations, erythrodermic psoriasis treatment, chronic urticaria diagnosis, and blistering disorders. Broader coverage extends to fungal infections, autoimmune conditions, neurologic cutaneous associations, and differential diagnosis of inflammatory and infectious dermatoses.
Dental: Dental academic knowledge integrates endodontic treatment methods, caries risk assessment in children, working length determination, orthodontic classification systems, composite resin polymerization shrinkage, impression material types, and dentine permeability factors. It spans restorative techniques, pediatric dentistry, periodontal surgery, biomaterials science, and occlusal mechanics, incorporating material properties, microbial pathology, and developmental anatomy.
